issues.detail: The Greek 'η δικη ζην ουκ ειασεν' (the judgment/punishment did not let him live) is rendered as 'hình phạt không cho phép sống'. While close, the Vietnamese phrasing implies a proactive prohibition ('không cho phép'), whereas the Greek 'ουκ ειασεν' (did not let live/permit life) in this context refers to the fact that he was not allowed to survive/live by the judgment. More importantly, the Vietnamese misses the nuance of the result: the man did not live because of the judgment.

The Greek 'παντως' (certainly/surely) is rendered as 'Chắc chắn', which is accurate, but the overall flow of the final clause in Vietnamese slightly obscures the causal link between the judgment and his death.
